note: Profession gap pass, grounded on 2026-09-27 with 52 fresh web searches (the first version was empty: its agent had no search budget). Every 'where' URL and every price URL below appeared in a search result during this task (seen_via: search). Prices are copied exactly from the search-result text; the URL on each step is the result page that text is attributed to. Direct page fetches are blocked by the network egress proxy (seemindia.org and peakframeworks.com were tried), so no price was checked on the page itself; Stage 2 must verify each one. reddit.com did not appear in any result, so no Reddit places are listed. Sizes are estimates unless a URL is given; measured supersets are cited inside the reasoning. Candidates checked first, as the earlier agent listed: freelance GRE/GMAT tutors, energy managers pursuing CEM or BEE certification, Big 4 transaction services / FDD associates moving to IB or PE. Three more rooms were added where the founder's depth is strong: RICS APC candidates (real estate), corporate development associates (deals), and valuation analysts pursuing a credential (valuation). Not pursued for lack of budget, not dropped for lack of grounding: freelance financial modellers on Upwork, warehouse operations managers taking ASCM certifications, power and energy traders.

rooms.name: Freelance GRE and GMAT tutors building a private tutoring practice
rooms.who: Independent tutors, often ex-test-prep-company instructors or high scorers, who sell GRE and GMAT tutoring by the hour through marketplaces (Wyzant, Upwork, Superprof, Preply) and their own referrals. They set their own rates, lose a quarter or a third of each lesson to platform fees, and try to move students onto their own site, scheduling and billing so they keep the whole fee. Many are in the US; a growing share are in India, Nigeria and the Middle East teaching online.

rooms.who_pays: The tutor pays out of lesson income: marketplace fees (Wyzant keeps a 25% platform fee; Preply takes between 18% and 33%), scheduling and invoicing software, a business course or coaching programme, and later agency software when they hire other tutors. Their students pay $35 to $60 an hour on Wyzant [measured, page not checked, https://blog.wyzant.com/how-much-does-tutoring-cost/] and $55 to $110 a session for GMAT [measured, page not checked, https://www.thumbtack.com/p/gmat-tutoring-cost], against $150 to $400 an hour at structured firms [measured, page not checked, https://menlocoaching.com/gre/best-gre-tutors/].

size.unit: freelance GRE and GMAT tutors actively selling lessons online, worldwide
size.reasoning: Wyzant alone has over 65,000 registered tutors across all subjects [measured, page not checked, https://brighterly.com/blog/wyzant-reviews/] and 'hundreds of independent GRE tutors' [measured, page not checked, https://menlocoaching.com/gre/best-gre-tutors/]. Adding GMAT tutors and the Upwork, Superprof, Preply and GMAT Club listings, plus India-based tutors who sell to the same students online, a few thousand active freelancers is a coarse guess; no count of GRE/GMAT-specific tutors was found. [thin]

rooms.name: Energy managers and auditors pursuing CEM or BEE energy-auditor certification
rooms.who: Plant, facility and consultancy engineers who must pass a certification exam to sign energy audits or hold the energy-manager title: India's BEE National Certification Examination (four papers, run by the National Productivity Council, 26th edition in 2026, applications close 30 July 2026) or the Association of Energy Engineers' Certified Energy Manager (CEM), taken in the US, the Gulf, Southeast Asia and Europe. They buy prep courses, sit the exam, then must renew (CEM every three years with 10 CEUs; BEE with a mandatory refresher course) and often stack ISO 50001 auditor training on top.

rooms.who_pays: The engineer pays personally for the exam fee and the prep course; employers sometimes pay for CEM training when the firm needs a certified signatory. Renewal fees, refresher courses and professional-body dues come out of the engineer's pocket. Consultancies that audit under India's PAT scheme need accredited auditors on staff, so the credential has direct earning value.

size.unit: engineers preparing for a BEE or CEM exam in a year, worldwide
size.reasoning: Over 40,000 professionals from over 100 countries have participated in AEE's CEM programme since 1981 [measured, page not checked, https://www.aeecenter.org/certified-energy-manager/], about 1,000 a year on average and more now that AEE runs monthly cohorts. BEE's exam is in its 26th edition with at least six paid coaching providers seen, which suggests several thousand candidates a year, but no BEE candidate count was found. [thin]

rooms.name: RICS APC candidates working toward chartered surveyor status
rooms.who: Graduate surveyors enrolled on the RICS Assessment of Professional Competence, mostly in the UK, the UAE and Saudi Arabia, in commercial property, valuation, quantity surveying and related pathways. Over two years of structured training they log experience, write a summary of experience and a case study, then face a 60-minute online final assessment interview that 41% fail. They pay RICS fees every year until they pass and buy coaching and mock interviews from a crowded market of ex-assessors.

rooms.name: Valuation analysts pursuing a business valuation credential (CVA, ABV, ASA or IBBI registered valuer)
rooms.who: Accountants and finance professionals who value private companies, shares and intangibles for deals, tax, disputes and insolvency, and who need a credential to sign reports: in the US the CVA (NACVA), ABV (AICPA) or ASA; in India the IBBI registered valuer licence for securities or financial assets, which needs 50 hours of mandatory training through a registered valuers organisation and an exam. They pay for training, exams, applications, memberships and data subscriptions, then recertify.

A stock of roughly 15,000 credentialed valuers across the two countries, with turnover and growth, implies a yearly inflow in the low thousands. [thin]
